reason: The submitted identities match the stated percentages and established chemistry: Q = Al, D = Na₃AlF₆, and AlF₃·3H₂O gives 39.16% water. However, identifying C additionally assumes that the precipitate is sodium-free, which the source does not state or independently establish. More seriously, the Lean Q/D proofs encode the requested answers in the singleton constructor IndustrialFluoridePair.hallHeroult and omit the two D percentage premises; they therefore do not substantively derive the identities from the problem. The individual target compiles with only permitted standard axioms, but the default project build also fails because IChO2026Problems/All.lean is missing.

coverage.evidence: Al is semantically consistent: Na₃AlF₆ has 12.8506787% Al using the printed masses, and cryolite is used in aluminium production. Formally, however, metal_q_identity merely eliminates IndustrialFluoridePair, whose only constructor already fixes q = Al and d = cryolite. It does not use or derive the 12.85% Q and 32.85% Na constraints, and the Element type omits almost all possible metals.

For assumed C = AlF₃, the proof correctly shows that every natural x consistent with 39.16 ± 0.005% is x = 3 without a finite search bound; the direct value is 39.1572724%. But hydrated_c_formula requires the unsupported premise c.sodium = 0 and an exact no-byproduct atom-addition interpretation of C + nNaF = D. The candidate itself proves that the stripped arithmetic also permits the distinct formal composition Na₂AlF₅·6H₂O.

Na₃AlF₆ reproduces 32.8506787% Na and 12.8506787% Al and is chemically consistent with the industrial clue. Nevertheless, compound_d_formula is tautological relative to the singleton IndustrialFluoridePair definition and contains neither percentage hypothesis. identified_answer_satisfies_problem_data establishes only that the preselected formula fits the data, not that the data identify it.

unsupported_assumptions: IndustrialFluoridePair is defined by the sole constructor hallHeroult : IndustrialFluoridePair cryolite .Al. Treating the source's general industrial-use clue as this singleton relation assumes both Q and D and an unproved uniqueness claim.
The Formula/Element universe admits Al as the only non-sodium metal, excluding other candidate metals before Q is derived.
The final C theorem assumes c.sodium = 0, although neither the prose nor the reaction diagram states that C is sodium-free.
ConvertsWithNaF assumes exact integral atom-count addition with no additional products; this is stronger than the printed statement that anhydrous C reacts with excess NaF to yield D.
The cited existence of AlF₃·3H₂O does not independently establish that it is the phase precipitated under the source's unspecified concentration and pH ≈ 4 conditions.
source_checks: TASK.json was read first. Its three exact requested output IDs and absence of preceding-part dependencies were confirmed.
The authorized SHA-256 values match T1_page-2.png, T1_page-3.png, and the 93-page theory_problem.pdf.
T1_page-3.png and original PDF page 8 were inspected directly. They state 39.16% water, 32.85% sodium, 12.85% Q, pH ≈ 4, NaF precipitation, and anhydrous C + excess NaF → D exactly as transcribed.
T1_page-2.png was inspected directly; it contains the preceding Part 1 molecular structures and supplies no additional T1-A4 constraint.
Blank student sheet PDF page 12 was inspected directly and requests exactly Q, C·xH₂O, and D, with no hidden annotations or extra constraints.
Original PDF page 5 was inspected directly and confirms H = 1.008, O = 16.00, F = 19.00, Na = 22.99, and Al = 26.98.
Independent arithmetic gives M(Na₃AlF₆) = 209.95 g mol⁻¹, 32.8506787% Na, 12.8506787% Al, and 39.1572724% water for AlF₃·3H₂O, all consistent with the printed two-decimal measurements.

Independent references confirm cryolite as Na₃AlF₆ used in aluminium production and confirm the existence/formula of aluminium fluoride trihydrate: [USGS](https://www.usgs.gov/centers/national-minerals-information-center/bauxite-and-alumina-statistics-and-information), [PubChem cryolite](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Sodium-hexafluoroaluminate), and [PubChem aluminium fluoride trihydrate](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Aluminium-fluoride-trihydrate). These references do not prove uniqueness of the industrial relation or the claimed precipitation phase.

A scan of all supplied Lean sources found no sorry, admit, custom axiom, unsafe declaration, or native_decide.
hydration_number_eq_three substantively proves x = 3 for arbitrary x : ℕ from the required half-quantum measurement interval and uses no unjustified search bound.
metal_q_identity and compound_d_formula do not use the source percentages and are immediate consequences of a constructor containing the answers.
identified_answer_satisfies_problem_data verifies consistency of preselected formulas but provides no uniqueness or identification theorem from the complete source data.
The default lake build fails because IChO2026Problems.lean imports the absent IChO2026Problems/All.lean; consequently the supplied umbrella/default target is not cleanly buildable.
